Hi all — technical appendix and capacity appendix attached. TL;DR on warm-standby behavior and residency controls below.

Technical summary:
- EU primary: model instances and KV cache live in eu-1 (physically isolated VPCs, EU KMS for data & model encryption). Audit logs and usage metrics are replicated to a read-only bucket also in EU to meet review needs.
- APAC warm-standby: pre-warmed inference instances in apac-1 with cold KV cache; when failover triggers (configurable policy: latency spike, region outage, or manual), traffic shifts to APAC pool. During failover we continue to write audit logs to EU-only storage via signed forwarding; raw request payloads are not stored in APAC.
- Key management: keys never leave EU. We use a proxy-based re-encryption approach for ephemeral session keys during failover so plaintext never crosses borders. HSM-backed KMS available as premium.
- SLAs & latency: normal steady-state latency from EU is 30–60ms p95 for current models; warm-standby failover adds 70–250ms depending on geo hops and cache coldness. We recommend a brief staged failover rehearsal after cutover.

Attachments: capacity-skus-appendix.xlsx, SOC2-evidence-summary-2025.pdf

Happy to walk through tomorrow on the technical call.

– Aditya
